beats.trigger: From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new, just the module title

beats.trigger: The hard part is not access; it is absorption.
beats.got: Sharing is about handing over context, not the agent, and the real obstacle is whether people take it up.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I already have one: the BI dashboards my team never opens.

beats.trigger: Name the likely adoption failure before it happens, including the social failure that's hardest to see
beats.got: A list of five verbs. The part about naming the failure up front is the useful bit.

beats.trigger: Two questions to warm up: who's the one person who came to mind just now? And what makes you hesitate about actually handing this to them?
beats.got: I thought of my pricing analyst, and I hesitate because she'd get a generic answer and quietly drop it.

beats.trigger: The starting question is theirs, not yours
beats.got: Start from the teammate's job, not from what I built. It's a consultant's instinct, but I don't usually apply it to my own tools.

beats.trigger: The test is specificity: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: A simple check on whether the job statement is real or generic. I can use it as written.

beats.trigger: Every picked candidate should name how it moves the teammate's outcome; infrastructure should appear only as a constraint.
beats.got: Choose the sharing shape by the outcome, not by what tooling we happen to have. 'Share the context' is the one that fits my team.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Find the one blocking obstacle, then write the technical plan and the people plan.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: A usable test for a root cause: if removing it only fixes itself, it isn't the root cause.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: The empty owner fields are the result. My team's shared context has no named owner, and that is my actual blocker.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure
beats.got: nothing new, just a pointer to the next exercise

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: Treat the plan as a bet to test, not a rollout to run.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: Roger Martin's question applied to a colleague. It makes me list what my analyst would have to believe to give up her private copy.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in one named person, one question and one test for Monday.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: nothing new, this is the infrastructure-as-constraint point again

beats.trigger: Industry analysts expect agent adoption to accelerate significantly over the coming years, which makes change management all the more important.
beats.got: nothing new, generic change-management filler

beats.trigger: The interview earned its keep when it found a third outcome past speed and quality: a dependency removed, an anxiety gone, a scope widened.
beats.got: A good interview finds an outcome beyond faster and better, such as a dependency removed or an anxiety gone. That could be the real job for my analyst.

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and you have handed them the shell of a thing whose contents are still on your disk and in your head.
beats.got: The value sits in the curated memory and the corrections, not in the instructions. That's why private prompt experiments don't spread.

beats.trigger: you recognise the new thing by what it resembles in the work you already do, and if it resembles nothing, you have nowhere to put it.
beats.got: Hand over something that looks like the teammate's existing work. A bit philosophical, but fair.

beats.trigger: Remember that adoption is everyone's responsibility.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Whether they pick it up is their decision, made for their own reasons, on a Tuesday you will not be in the room for.
beats.got: I can't mandate this onto fourteen people. I can only make the thing worth picking up.

beats.trigger: The before-and-after quote is how you know the sharpening reached the file, not just the summary.
beats.got: Make the agent show the actual before and after lines, so a claimed improvement is checkable.

beats.trigger: The artifact: the sharpened sharing file itself, plus one line in your Module 7 next-step file naming the first move.
beats.got: nothing new, just the housekeeping for what to save

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: nothing new, the third time this has been said

beats.trigger: Test one assumption. Ask for one name. Talk to one person.
beats.got: A small, specific job for the week that makes me go and talk to someone.

beats.trigger: What comes back from that contact is Module 8's raw material.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Don't hand a teammate my agent. The thing worth sharing is the curated context, and my team has no shared place for it and no named owner.
Start from the teammate's job and the outcome they want, then pick the sharing shape. A people plan with UNASSIGNED owners is a finding, not a finished rollout.
Ask what would have to be true for a teammate to drop what they use today, and test that with one conversation before building anything.

monday.move: Ask the analyst who builds the pilot-cohort brief how she does it today and what would make her use a shared context folder instead of her private copy. Test that one assumption.
monday.who: The analyst in the pricing working group who prepares the pilot-cohort numbers
monday.when: Monday morning, 30 minutes before the pricing working group meets
monday.stop_condition: If her own copy already works and she gives no reason to switch, I stop building the shared folder and ask what job she would hire it for instead.
monday.blocker: There is no shared place for the context files and nobody owns it. I have to decide who that is, and it is still UNASSIGNED.

misconception.why: The module says the value lives in the curated memory and corrections, not in the instructions, so better prompts are the shell. I haven't tried it on my team yet, so I'm not fully convinced.

one_line: Good on 'share the context, not the agent' and on the empty-owner finding, but the point gets made three times and the adoption boilerplate paragraphs could go.
